Use the model above to determine the missing fraction in the following division problem.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/14cdf48e441388f15954ecb2ffbe7e56d653abb1dfaa3d95b2abd573e6318cca.svg)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/e60ebf4ac02326cff610f1d4238bb2b8c16062aaa8a50c7cc040631e65d3a5b0.png)
question.worked_solution:
Let's start by interpreting our model:

- The model shows $2$ wholes split into sixths.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/6c4328991ef5f89f91b3df5b4d43f8034d58249442700d59c2d842a44c9e8cda.png)

- There are $\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{5}$ sixths in each group, with $\bbox[2pt, Moccasin]{2}$ remaining.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/e08a28fee137c40615d7261b6282dce8dd0392084a8d801f9cc848364a3ad0f5.png)

Note the following: 

- There are $\color{red}2$ full groups.

- There are $\bbox[2pt, Moccasin]{2}$ sixths left over out of a possible group of $\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{5}.$ So the fractional part of our answer is 

$$
\dfrac{\bbox[2pt, Moccasin]{2}}{\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{5}}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
2 \div \dfrac{5}{6} = {\color{red}{2}} \, \dfrac{\bbox[2pt, Moccasin]{2}}{\bbox[2pt, lightgray]{5}}.
$$
